text: requirements briefed to DOE. The SMC-V1 design and progress was effectively communicated to DOE during the monthly meetings. The cutting of glass fiber and TCF (different precursor based) was illustrated via videos. The wet- out challenges for TCF in SMC-V1 was also conveyed  Milestone 6.23.3.2 Demonstrated continuous operation of SMC line (between 12”-24” width) for at least one hour with one product form for recycled or textile carbon fibers. (January 2020). The SMC line was run continually for 12” in width using the Kaltex precursor. The cut quality 73 for ½” and 1” was excellent as illustrated in the cutting section. In terms of production of SMC with the TCF, limited demonstration was conducted with SMC-V1 and because the wet out was not sufficient, it took 5-6 months to make the modifications described i.e. the 14-roll station compaction roll. This enabled producing TCF with good wet-out. This was a 30-min run for 30 wt% TCF.  Milestone 6.23.5.1 Produce ≥ 10 flat panels ≥ 1 ft2 x 1/8±1/32” thick, molded at pressure ≥ 1,200 psi from textile carbon fiber SMC. This goal was adequately met. Appendix A summarizes the test results from the TCF SMC for tensile, flex, ILSS and Izod impact.  Milestone 6.23.5.2 Produce ≥ 10 flat panels ≥ 1 ft2 x 1/8±1/32” thick, molded at pressure ≥ 1,200 psi from recycled carbon fiber SMC made for demonstrating. Testing has been performed on rCF consolidated mats mimicking SMC like panels. Hybrid SMC with glass fiber SMC and rCF mats were produced and a comprehensive data set was generated and reported in the Hybrid SMC section.  Milestone 6.23.6.2 Experimental data, acquired by ASTM standard tests, demonstrated the mechanical property requirements of milestone 6.23.2.1. This has been compiled in the Hybrid SMC section.  Milestone 6.23.6.3 Business case and embodied energy analysis briefed to DOE (August 2020) The Simapro license renewal set us back on this milestone and it was not completed.
